roles.image-greyscale: thumbnails are desaturated B&W; their natural tone is the only imagery 'color'
roles.project-hover-chroma: per-case accent hues (pink #ff71cb, gold #cc9933, green #53bb89, …) belong to individual project views/WebGL, NOT the chrome

stack: WebGL/<canvas> + requestAnimationFrame (hand-rolled, no library globals detected)

notes: Screenshot is ground truth; raw profile is noisy. THE SIGNATURE COLOR is a desaturated sage-grey #bac4b8 (raw rgb(186,196,184), the #1 color, 224 uses) used for ALL chrome text on a near-black #1e1e1e ground (raw rgb(30,30,30)) — this is NOT a white-on-black page, and naming fg as sage (not #fff) is the whole point. The raw color list's pink/gold/green/purple/red entries are per-project case accents / WebGL output, not part of the system, so they are dropped from roles. ONE weight only (raw fontWeight 400, 2057 uses) — no bold anywhere; emphasis is scale + value, never weight. Two families: a heavy CONDENSED display grotesque (raw alias 'jws', 1436 uses) for the wordmark, and a tabular monospace (raw alias 'TNY', 621 uses) for the tick-readout + micro-labels; both named neutrally because the raw aliases are obfuscated webfont names. Display scale is genuinely extreme: raw shows 337.5px (~16.1rem, the giant wordmark, 572 uses) and 257.5px (~9rem) with heavy negative tracking (raw letterSpacing -8.1px ≈ -0.05em on display); kept as a hero-only token, not a magic number. Micro UI sits at 10–12px (raw 0.625–0.75rem) with positive tracking 0.2px on labels. Tightest leading is the display lock-up (raw 253px line on 337px text ≈ 0.75). Radius 0 and shadow none everywhere — depth comes from edge-bleed layering of the slat gallery and a faint edge mask, never elevation. Motion: the only authored CSS transitions are raw 500ms with easings 'ease' + 'cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94)' (easeOutQuad) for hover/UI; the heavy drag-scroll inertia + WebGL hovers on thumbnails are JS/GL and INVISIBLE to computed styles — captured only as 2 <canvas> nodes + a persistent rAF loop (604 calls/pass) + 1 mousemove listener. This is NOT a scroll-choreography site: 0 @keyframes, 0 CSS animation rules, no IntersectionObserver, no scroll listeners, and just 1 scroll effect (a position→fixed pin on the project-viewer main). The 4 scroll frames are pixel-identical (fixed single-screen stage; motion is drag/hover, which scroll-stepping can't show), so the motion block is grounded in probe counts + the pinned-main DOM, not frames; the recorded 'entrance' spans (1.00→1.00 index digits) are dropped as from==to noise. prefers-reduced-motion is NOT respected (prmRules:0) — the headline a11y defect, since the GL strip is the only path to the work. The 'inertial-drag-strip' and 'webgl-thumbnail-hover-reveal' techniques have no exact corpus recipe (patterns_to_build); related existing patterns are webgl-thumbnail-sphere, inset-canvas-stage, edge-bleed-portrait-strip, tick-scrubber-indicator, sticky-pin-scrollytelling. Space base ~8px but operative gaps are the 30px (3.75-ish) chrome inset (raw paddingInline 30px, 262 uses) and large vertical voids around the centered strip.
